title: A Fake Fight in a Library Caught the Silk Road Founder

narration: Silk Road: a dark-web drug empire built on anonymity.
A fake fight in a public library caught its founder.

sources.claim_text: Silk Road was an online black market that ran as a hidden service on the Tor network from early 2011 (the complaint: activity from about January/February 2011) until the FBI seized the site and arrested its operator on 1-2 October 2013; buyers paid in bitcoin. Narration: 'a dark-web drug empire built on anonymity' / 'It ran on Tor and Bitcoin'. No drugs or listings are drawn.

On 1 October 2013, in the science-fiction section of the Glen Park branch of the San Francisco Public Library, Kiernan stood behind Ulbricht to photograph his screen while two other agents posed as a bickering couple to create a diversion; when he looked up, agents grabbed the laptop before he could close it, and he was arrested without resisting. Narration: 'two agents staged a loud fight behind him' / 'He looked up. An agent grabbed the laptop'. Headline: 'A FAKE FIGHT IN A LIBRARY / CAUGHT THE SILK ROAD FOUNDER'. The agents are generic and unnamed on screen.

narration: It ran on Tor and Bitcoin: over 200 million dollars in sales.

sources.claim_text: Silk Road was an online black market that ran as a hidden service on the Tor network from early 2011 (the complaint: activity from about January/February 2011) until the FBI seized the site and arrested its operator on 1-2 October 2013; buyers paid in bitcoin. Narration: 'a dark-web drug empire built on anonymity' / 'It ran on Tor and Bitcoin'. No drugs or listings are drawn.

The Justice Department's 2015 sentencing release says Silk Road's users bought and sold more than $200 million in illegal goods and that Ulbricht took commissions of more than $13 million; prosecutors' trial estimate was more than $213 million (2011-2013). The 2013 FBI complaint had converted about 9.5 million bitcoins of revenue to roughly $1.2 billion at then-current exchange rates (CBS; Fox): a conversion, not a measured dollar sum, so narration and the card use the DOJ figure 'over $200 million'.

narration: An IRS agent started with a Google search.

overlays.text: IRS CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION / STEP ONE: A GOOGLE SEARCH

sources.claim_text: CARD ONLY: the site's operator was known to investigators only by the handle 'Dread Pirate Roberts' (DPR).

IRS criminal-investigation special agent Gary Alford (not named on screen), working with the DEA/strike force in New York, searched Google for the earliest mentions of Silk Road and found that in January 2011, shortly after the site started, a user called 'altoid' had posted about Silk Road on the Bitcointalk.org and Shroomery.org forums (NYT, Dec 2015; his trial testimony, Jan 2015). Narration: 'An IRS agent started with a Google search.' / 'A 2011 forum post by altoid advertised Silk Road.' The screen is a generic, illegible forum page.

sources.claim_text: In altoid's posting history, a later Bitcointalk post seeking a developer (its exact date not in any extract) told applicants to email an address at Gmail that was Ross Ulbricht's own name; with a search warrant the IRS then obtained the account's email from Google. Narration: 'Later, altoid gave his own Gmail address: Ross Ulbricht.' The address itself is never spoken or shown (card: 'A GMAIL ADDRESS · HIS OWN NAME').

Ross William Ulbricht, then 29, of San Francisco (originally from Austin, Texas), was charged in Manhattan federal court as the site's operator; he is drawn only as an anonymous silhouette (characters/figures/sr32_ulbricht.json).

sources.claim_text: Agents wanted to arrest him with his laptop open and unencrypted: FBI computer scientist Thomas Kiernan testified 'We waited for an opportunity to arrest the defendant with his laptop open to avoid encryption'; the undercover agent (Jared Der-Yeghiayan) said the aim was to get the computer 'in an open, unencrypted state'; closing the lid would have encrypted its contents. Narration: 'Close the lid and it would encrypt. Agents needed it open.'

On 1 October 2013, in the science-fiction section of the Glen Park branch of the San Francisco Public Library, Kiernan stood behind Ulbricht to photograph his screen while two other agents posed as a bickering couple to create a diversion; when he looked up, agents grabbed the laptop before he could close it, and he was arrested without resisting. Narration: 'two agents staged a loud fight behind him' / 'He looked up. An agent grabbed the laptop'. Headline: 'A FAKE FIGHT IN A LIBRARY / CAUGHT THE SILK ROAD FOUNDER'. The agents are generic and unnamed on screen.

Photographs of the screen showed him logged into Silk Road's 'mastermind' administrator panel as Dread Pirate Roberts; at that moment he was chatting with an undercover agent over the site's staff chat; the laptop's one account, 'Frosty', was signed in. Narration: 'still logged in as the admin.' Card: 'LOGGED IN AS THE ADMIN · DREAD PIRATE ROBERTS'. The screen drawn is a generic dark panel with illegible blocks.

In 2025 he was pardoned, and released.

sources.claim_text: On Wednesday 4 February 2015 a federal jury in Manhattan convicted Ulbricht on all seven counts (including narcotics trafficking, continuing criminal enterprise, computer hacking and money-laundering conspiracies) after less than a day of deliberation.

On Friday 29 May 2015 U.S. District Judge Katherine B. Forrest sentenced him to life in prison without the possibility of parole (two life terms plus 20, 15 and 5 years, all concurrent). Narration: 'life without parole.'

On 21 January 2025 President Donald Trump announced a 'full and unconditional pardon' of Ross Ulbricht (after 11 years in prison), and he was released from the federal prison in Tucson, Arizona. Narration states it as fact only: 'In 2025 he was pardoned, and released.' No opinion is given; the burned-in end question asks the viewer.

narration: Built on anonymity. Brought down by a fake fight.
